title: Boolean Rank via Monomial Ideals: monomials in the determinantal ideal correspond to isolated sets (printed as Theorem 4.13)
author: Juliann Geraci, Alexander B. Kunin, Alexandra Seceleanu
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4.13 (source0.tex lines 653--655, source label thm: monomials=isolated): if a square-free monomial of degree s at least 2 lies in the s-th determinantal ideal of a Boolean matrix, then its entries form an isolated set. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 656--704 (49 lines, one adjacent proof environment), together with the complete proof of the base-case lemma (lines 616--649). The argument is a genuine induction: the induction step expands the relevant minor of the generic matrix along its determinant, uses the fact that the monomial sets of distinct maximal minors are disjoint so that nothing can cancel, forces every non-identity permutation term to vanish, concludes that the principal (s-1)-minor is still a monomial generator of the (s-1)-st determinantal ideal, applies the induction hypothesis, and then runs the same argument at every index to show that every pair of the s entries is an isolated pair. The substantive content is the cancellation analysis inside the determinant expansion and the reduction of the s-fold isolation conclusion to the pairwise statement; neither is an unpacking of definitions. H2: a complete original research-paper theorem, moderately short, whose proof is a genuinely technical inductive argument.
